sources.citation: The Rosetta Project. 2010. Wanap Swadesh List. The Rosetta Project: A Long Now Foundation Library of Human Language (archive.org item rosettaproject_wnp_swadesh-1, file, uploaded 2010-09-16, CC-BY 3.0). c. 50-item Swadesh list for Wanap [wnp] in two transcriptions; no compiler or source named in the item metadata (forms agree with Laycock 1968 as reproduced on TransNewGuinea.org).
sources.note: Nothing. Bare gloss:form list (arm: pam.. two: poyomp), each gloss given in a practical spelling (e-diaeresis, ng, backslash for glottal stop) and again in IPA (schwa, eng, glottal stop, length mark); vowel length and glottal stop are marked but there are no stress, accent or tone marks and no prose of any kind. The companion holds only upload headers (no source attribution).

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1975. The Torricelli Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 767-780. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Kayik appears only in the Palei Family list (769 speakers, p. 768). The family-level phonological characterisation (p. 769: three positions of articulation, usually no voicing contrast, five to eight vowels, high proportion of fricatives, illustrated from Olo) says nothing about stress, accent or tone.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU. Entry 31 'KAYIK (Menandon, Minendon, Wanap)', p. 11.
sources.note: Nothing. The Kayik entry (p. 11, p. 15) gives only villages (Mai, Wanali, Yambil, Kuwalvu, Weranyuwok, Yiliwambil), 769 speakers, test list DCL67 and a pointer to Laycock 1968:14. The Torricelli Phylum introduction (p. 7) says only that the phonology 'differs from that of most other Sepik groups in permitting vowel sequences, and in having a large (5 to 8) number of vowel phonemes'; no mention of stress or tone anywhere for Kayik.
Nothing. Only Laycock 1968 (p. 48) is cited, as a subclassification comment; no descriptive references. Alternative names Kayik, Menandon, Minendon; ELP lists it as 'Kayik'.
